problems.title: The uniqueness proof uses false graph and bottleneck identities
problems.evidence: Path partition beta0 difference-1 vs edge difference1; cycle adds edge without H0 death; repeated bars have dB0.5 independent of count
problems.assumptions: Standard finite graph homology and bottleneck distance; both common-vertex and incident-vertex conventions considered
problems.counterevidence: Empirical useful fits remain possible; stronger global identification assumptions could alter theorem
problems.impact: Central ground-truth uniqueness guarantee not established
problems.repair: Restate assumptions and prove actual surrogate with correct graph/metric relations
problems.repair_verification: Finite counterexamples independently executed; replacement theorem not verified

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Read and actually viewed physical p.6 Theorem3.4/Definition3.2 and p.16 complete AppendixC proof. The theorem assumes smaller oracle rationale and information loss for each proper subgraph of that oracle, not unique sufficiency among all other edge subsets. Both ordinary common-vertex and isolate-discarding graph conventions were examined.
independent_check.decisive_check: The first containment implication does not follow from minimality within one oracle: an alternative informative subgraph or redundant copy is not excluded. Independently, beta0=V-E+beta1 gives the four-vertex path partition rationale{01},noise{12,23} beta0 values3,2, hence difference -1 versus printed edge difference+1. With isolates removed both have beta0=1. In the triangle partition rationale{03,13},noise{01,12,02}, noise has3 edges versus2 but both have2 H0 merges; one noise edge creates H1. Bottleneck-to-empty for n copies(0,1) is max over n equal diagonal costs=.5, independent of n. These hand derivations agree with the frozen verified independent_check_output.json without rerunning it.
independent_check.counterevidence: The path example is an acyclic connected full graph, so cycle exclusion cannot rescue the sign/count identity. Repeated finite bars are a diagnostic of the asserted metric identity, not a complete counterexample to the final neural optimization theorem; essential bars require a separately specified convention. Empirical utility is not contradicted. A different global identification assumption could repair the first implication, but does not repair the later independent identities.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Major retained because the claimed unique ground-truth optimizer relies on all these reductions. Distributional Wasserstein, per-graph bottleneck counts, learned large homology scaling, and a finite witness lower bound are not interchangeable maximization objectives. A lower bound can change maximizers; arbitrary learned scaling must also respect the claimed Lipschitz constant. Restating the theorem and proving the actual surrogate are substantive repairs not verified here.
anchors: page_16.txt AppendixC first paragraph and beta0/dB equality

problems.title: Rational Hat vectorization lacks required bottleneck Lipschitz property
problems.evidence: A bar(0,epsilon) approaching diagonal has kernel value tending0.5 but dBtoempty epsilon/2; ratio diverges
problems.assumptions: Displayed kernel with admissible c0,r1 on variable-cardinality diagram space
problems.counterevidence: Pointwise smoothness or empirical usefulness does not imply diagram-space Lipschitz; restricted domain might support a different bound
problems.impact: Claimed computable Wasserstein lower bound and theoretical link not justified
problems.repair: Use proven stable domain/function class, enforce Lipschitz normalization and justify attention aggregation
problems.repair_verification: Exact limit and numerical values; no replacement construction verified

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Actually viewed p.6 Rational Hat equation: Euclidean norm is subscript2, not squared norm; parameters c in R2 and r in R are unconstrained as stated. Proposition3.3 requires functions one-Lipschitz on diagram space under bottleneck distance.
independent_check.decisive_check: For c=(0,0),r=1, singleton P={(0,e)} and empty Q, 0<e<1, the feature difference is 1/(1+e)-1/(2-e), tending .5, while the standard bottleneck distance is e/2. Thus ratio tends infinity; at e=1e-6 it is999997.50000175. Adding a shared persistent bar makes both diagrams nonempty with the same feature difference and distance e/2. Even using the erroneous printed projection would give cost e and still a divergent ratio. This defect therefore survives the local P3 correction.
independent_check.counterevidence: For actual one-Lipschitz witnesses, any coupling bounds the absolute expectation difference by its expected cost; Proposition3.3 itself is sound. Pointwise smoothness, fixed batch tensors, and empirical usefulness do not imply diagram stability under near-diagonal insertion/deletion. A restricted finite diagram domain could admit another constant but no such restriction is stated. Two identical valid witnesses can each attain distance d, making their unnormalized sum2d; two-head selection alone is not a one-Lipschitz normalization.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Major for the central computable Wasserstein lower-bound claim. A diagonal-vanishing construction with appropriate cardinality/domain bounds and constrained aggregation needs proof. No stable replacement architecture was implemented or certified; the empirical regularizer may still be useful.
anchors: page_06.txt Proposition3.3, Rational Hat equation and top-2 maxima paragraph

problems.title: Wrong closest diagonal point in bottleneck definition
problems.location: AppendixB DefinitionB1 p15; old supplement p7
problems.assumptions: Standard birth-death coordinates and infinity norm as explicitly stated
problems.counterevidence: Likely local definition typo; code uses PH backend rather than direct printed matching formula
problems.impact: Printed definition incorrect; historical numerical effect not established
problems.repair: Use midpoint diagonal projection and half-persistence cost
problems.repair_verification: Algebraic and finite numeric correction verified

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Actually viewed physical p.15 DefinitionB.1; p=(p1,p2) is ordinary birth/death coordinates and the metric explicitly uses infinity norm. The printed diagonal projection is (p2-p1,p2-p1).
independent_check.decisive_check: For any diagonal coordinate t, max(abs(b-t),abs(d-t)) is at least abs(d-b)/2 by the triangle inequality, with equality at t=(b+d)/2. For b=.1,d=.7 the printed t=.6 costs.5, while the true midpoint .4 costs.3. This is a literal mathematical error, not extraction loss.
independent_check.counterevidence: The inspected release computes persistent representations via a backend rather than directly implementing the printed partial-matching formula. No historical metric computation using the typo was established. Therefore the isolated definition repair is Minor; its severity is not discounted merely because it is in an appendix.
independent_check.dependency_severity_repair: Minor retained with exact local midpoint/half-persistence correction verified algebraically. P1 and P2 were checked using the correct metric and remain independently valid; repairing this typo does not establish the uniqueness or Lipschitz results.
